scope: Proposition 2.4 (The spherical Springer test) of the manuscript “Ramanujan-Arthur Decompositions of Cuspidal Functions at Full Finite Level” (preprints/Ramanujan-Arthur-Decompositions-of-Cuspidal-Functions-at-Full-Finite-Level-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 014 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b4b0cfe23007d159), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let For forget L+G-equivariance to Iu- equivariance on GrG, without changing the underlying complex, and let Av∗ be its right adjoint. Put Wη = Jη ⋆ δ0. For every integral weight η in the closed costandard chamber, derived Satake identifies Av∗ Wη with Rπ∗O e N (η)  sh , π : f N −→ b g. The subscript means that coherent degree a and polynomial degree b are assigned total degree a + 2b. This is an equivalence of ordinary equivariant dg S-modules. The S-action is polyno- mial restriction along π, and the assertion is compatible with tensoring by representations and with all morphisms between free Satake labels. The displayed convention introduces no extra shift. Any smooth-pullback normalization of For changes the formula only by a fixed shift and Tate twist, independent of η.
